title: Tool capability scope
task_statement: Attach only the tools a task needs, and scope each tool to its job. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Tool surface scope
components.first_principle: Each attached tool is a permission, a token cost, and a selection choice, so the set should hold only what the task calls.

nodes.label: Scoped tools array for this task
Claude model picks a tool by name

steps: List the tools the task calls before you attach any tool. (Inference)
Remove each tool that the task never calls. (Inference)
Merge related operations into fewer tools with an action parameter.
Cap or gate each tool that writes or deletes data. (Inference)
Set allowlists or denylists in the mcp_toolset configuration.
Keep the default always_ask policy for MCP tools that change data in Managed Agents.
Review the tool list again when the task changes. (Inference)
pros: Removal ends the permission itself, and a log entry does not.
Fewer schemas reduce the tokens sent on every call.
One name for each job reduces confusion between similar tools.
cons: A removed tool leaves edge cases without a path, so the team needs a new route.
A coarse vendor tool can force a broad scope.
A scoped tool can still fire at the wrong moment.
use_when: One agent serves one task with a defined set of tools.
A tool can write, delete, or return sensitive data.
Two tools have near-identical names or descriptions.
do_not_use_when: A single-user local tool holds no production data and no secrets.
A known workflow still needs the tool that you plan to remove.
The tool set already holds only the tools that every request uses.

constraints.choice: Remove tools the task never calls from every request. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Defer the rest with tool search when the set grows large.

constraints.choice: Use tool search when the set has 10 or more tools.
constraints.combination: Keep the 3 to 5 most used tools non-deferred.

constraints.choice: Keep write tools on always_ask in MCP toolsets.
constraints.combination: Use always_allow only for a trusted read-only MCP server. (Inference)

constraints.choice: In Claude Code, deny rules apply first, then ask rules, then allow rules.
constraints.combination: Add a deny rule for a blocked tool. An allow rule cannot override it.

constraints.choice: Record tool decisions and results in your audit log. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Use the audit log to review removals, not to replace them. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D3.1. Expect a scenario with an over-broad tool set and one wrong call. The credited answer removes or scopes the unneeded tool. A log entry alone is not the fix. (Inference)
components.trap: Full audit logs on a broad tool set look like the safe fix. The permission stays attached, so the next wrong call still runs.
components.decision_rule: Remove or scope each tool the task does not need before you add any monitoring.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario names an unneeded write capability, pick removal, a cap, or an approval gate.

components.name: Tool search with deferred tools
components.first_principle: Deferred tools stay out of the first prompt, and the API adds the found tools when the model searches for them.

nodes.label: Your app with full tool catalog

edges.label: deferred tools stay out of prefix

steps: Add the tool search tool to the tools array without defer_loading.
Set defer_loading to true on each tool that few requests use.
Keep at least one non-deferred tool, normally the search tool itself.
Let the API return up to 5 matches for each search by default.
Put a cache breakpoint on a non-deferred tool, not on a deferred one.
Add a system prompt line that lists the tool categories you offer.
pros: Only the tools a request needs enter the context.
The API expands discovered tools into full definitions automatically.
Deferred tools leave the cached tool prefix unchanged.
cons: Each search adds a step before the tool call. (Inference)
A deferred tool cannot carry cache_control, and the API returns an error.
Search quality depends on clear names and descriptions.
use_when: The catalog holds hundreds of tools from several MCP servers.
Tool definitions take more than 10k tokens per request.
Most requests use only a few tools from a large catalog.
do_not_use_when: Every request uses every tool in a small set.
The tool definitions are under 100 tokens in total.
The model is Claude Opus 4.1 or an earlier model, which lacks tool search.

constraints.choice: Defer tools that few requests use.
constraints.combination: Keep frequent tools non-deferred to avoid extra search round trips.

constraints.choice: Accept one extra search step for large catalogs. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Use standard tool use when the set is small.

constraints.choice: Allow up to 10,000 deferred tools in one request.
constraints.combination: Claude can set a limit from 1 to 10,000 in its search input.

constraints.choice: Use clear names and keyword-rich descriptions for each deferred tool.
constraints.combination: Use a shared name prefix such as github_ for one service.

constraints.choice: Monitor which tools the model discovers.
constraints.combination: Rewrite descriptions for tools that the model never finds.

components.exam_tie: D3.1. Expect a scenario with a large tool library and high token cost. The credited answer defers rarely used tools and keeps frequent tools in the prompt. (Inference)
components.trap: A longer system prompt that lists every tool looks like a fix. It keeps every schema in the first prompt.
components.decision_rule: Defer each tool that few requests use, and keep the most used tools non-deferred.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario shows 10 or more tools and high cost, pick tool search over a longer prompt.

components.name: Tool definition quality
components.first_principle: Clear, few, and consistently named tool definitions give the model the fewest wrong picks.

nodes.label: Tool author writes description and schema
Strict mode grammar limit per request

steps: Describe each tool by its purpose and the conditions that call it.
State in each description what the tool does not return.
Group related actions under one tool with an action parameter when they share inputs.
Prefix each tool name with its service or resource name.
Return only the fields the model needs for its next step.
Add input_examples for tools with nested or format-sensitive inputs.
pros: Clear descriptions are the largest single factor in tool performance, per the docs.
Consistent prefixes make search and selection unambiguous.
Compact responses save context on every turn.
cons: Long descriptions add tokens to every request.
Consolidated tools need more conditional logic in the input schema.
Input examples add tokens on every request.
use_when: Two tools return similar data and the model picks the wrong one.
A tool takes nested or format-sensitive input.
The model needs a stable identifier from one call to the next.
do_not_use_when: A tool has a one-line job with a clear name and no inputs.
A consolidated action would mix reads with destructive writes.
The set already holds a few clear tools.

constraints.choice: Write descriptions of at least 3 to 4 sentences for each tool, more for a complex tool.
constraints.combination: Use input_examples only for tools with complex inputs.

constraints.choice: Use stable slugs or UUIDs in tool responses.
constraints.combination: Remove fields the next step never reads.

constraints.choice: Keep destructive actions in separate tools with their own gates. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Share one read tool across several services only when the data scope matches.

constraints.choice: Limit strict tools to 20 per request.
constraints.combination: Leave non-strict tools outside this limit.

native_services.text: Not in source for platform-specific tool definition limits. The strict tool limit is documented on the structured outputs page.

components.exam_tie: D3.1. Expect a scenario where the model picks a near-duplicate tool. The credited answer merges or renames tools, not a longer prompt. (Inference)
components.trap: A system prompt rule that says to pick the right search tool looks like a fix. Two tools with the same job still split the model choice.
components.decision_rule: Give each job one tool name and one description, and merge tools that do the same job.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario shows two similar search tools, pick the option that merges them or renames them for distinct jobs.

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Does the task ever need this tool?} -->|No| X[Remove from the request]
  A -->|Yes| B{Does the tool write or delete data?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Cap the writes or add an approval gate]
  B -->|No| D{Ten or more tools in the set?}
  C --> D
  D -->|Yes| E[Use tool search with deferred tools]
  D -->|No| F[Attach with standard tool use]
  E --> G{Does another tool do the same job?}
  F --> G
  G -->|Yes| H[Merge the tools into one name]
  G -->|No| I[Keep the tool with a clear description]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  S[Task tools only] --> R[Remove unused tools]
  R --> M[Merge same-job tools]
  S --> W[Cap or gate writes]
  S --> D[Defer rare tools]
  D --> K[Keep frequent tools non-deferred]
  S --> P[Deny then ask then allow]
  W --> A[Approval on write tools]
  S --> L[Logs record, removal blocks]
